newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CNI groups sees Brazil '97 trade gap at $10-12 bln.
newsitem.headline: CNI groups sees Brazil '97 trade gap at $10-12 bln.

text.p: Brazil is heading for a trade deficit of between $10 billion and $12 billion this year, said the president of the private National Industry Confederation, Fernando Bezerra.
Bezerra said the CNI had previously forecast a trade deficit of $6 billion in 1997, but was increasing its predictions given the fast pace of import growth.
"We are worried about the speed with which the trade deficit is growing," Bezerra told reporters at a news conference to announce industrial output figures for February.
Recalling comments by Central Bank director Gustavo Franco, who had said that Brazil could cope with a trade gap of up to $15 billion this year, Bezerra said: "I hope he is right."

The figures published by the CNI Tuesday show industrial sales rising 6.49 percent in the first two months of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996. Imports in the first quarter, however, were 25 percent higher than in the same 1996 period.
Bezerra urged the government to create more incentives for exports, principally through better financing terms.
